Team —

Context: demand from product orgs (LLM infra, Ads ranking, and Platform) indicates we need to expand the FY27 intern-to-new-grad conversion plan to avoid losing top interns to competing offers. I ran a quick quota projection (attached) and am asking for sign-off on both headcount and targeted pay-band adjustments so TA can finalize offer paperwork by end of month.

- Approve increase of conversion offers from the previously planned 30 to 45 total (across Eng orgs).
- Approve targeted base-band bump: +$5k base for top-tier conversions in LLM and Infra teams only.

Why: 6 interns (LLM infra) have competing verbal offers at +$7–10k ranges; if we keep current bands we risk losing the most mission-critical talent. Numbers in the attached model show net headcount cost delta and potential revenue impact of losing these hires.

Deadline: please confirm by EOD Tue 2026-11-17 so TA can lock offers and trigger background checks and payroll integration.

Attachments: intern_quota_model_v3.xlsx (workbook with breakdown by team, candidate priority tiers)

I'll follow up with the committee if helpful.

Jasmine / Karthik —

I ran a compensation-impact delta and attached a one-page summary for quick review (comp_impact_prodcalc.pdf). TL;DR: a blanket +$5k base for all conversions would cost ~ $415k annual run-rate across the 45 hires; targeted +$5k for just the 12 high-priority LLM/Infra hires brings that to ~ $112k run-rate.

Recommendations:
- Approve targeted base-band bump for LLM + Infra only (12 hires). This minimizes comp drift and addresses the acute retention risk.
- For the remaining conversions, do $3k sign-on (taxable one-time) to be paid within the first payroll cycle — easier to reverse if needed and doesn't change salary bands long-term.
- Consider a $2k retention bonus at the 12-month mark for the most mission-critical roles (paid prorated).

I can support with the updated offer language and total comp letters once finance confirms budget.

Attachment: comp_impact_prodcalc.pdf

--Evelyn
